overview.headline: How cosine works as a function of angle in similar triangles

keyPoints.point: A function means variable value depends uniquely on different variable value
keyPoints.quote: the value of one variable in a problem depends uniquely on the value of another variable in the problem.

keyPoints.point: Trigonometric functions relate triangle sides and angles
keyPoints.quote: The trigonometric functions sine, cosine, and tangent relate the various sides and angles of a triangle.

keyPoints.point: Black triangle cosine is equal to divided side values
keyPoints.quote: For the black triangle, the cosine of “b” is equal to x divided by y.

keyPoints.point: Cosine value depends only on angle value not side length
keyPoints.quote: The value of cosine “b” just depends on the value of “b” and not the length of the sides that form “b”.

keyTerms.gloss: idea where a quantity depends uniquely on a different quantity
keyTerms.quote: An important mathematical concept is the idea of function

keyTerms.gloss: ratio of adjacent side to hypotenuse for a given triangle angle
keyTerms.quote: For the black triangle, the cosine of “b” is equal to x divided by y.

keyTerms.gloss: trigonometric function relating sides and angles of triangle
keyTerms.quote: The trigonometric functions sine, cosine, and tangent relate the various sides and angles of a triangle.

keyTerms.gloss: longest side length opposite right angle in red triangle
keyTerms.quote: For the red triangle, the length of the hypotenuse “h” is 2y, twice the hypotenuse of the black triangle.
